description:
## Goal

Treat runtime equality assertions as constraints only. `AssertSame { source, value }` reads two already-defined values and proves they are semantically equal; it must not create a physical/value-origin definition edge in either direction.

## Proven defect

During the ticket-scoped adversarial review of fz-tfn.64, this valid production program stack-overflowed on interpreter, JIT, and AOT:

```fz
fn main() do
  x = 42
  ^x = x
  x
end
```

`ExecutableFacts::step_transport_origins` records `value -> LocalValue(source)` for `AssertSame`. Here both operands are the same existing value, producing a self-cycle in downstream origin traversal. More generally, structurally equal but separately allocated values satisfy equality without sharing allocation identity, so the edge is false even when it is acyclic.

The independent assertion inventory confirms this is not a missing cycle guard: `AssertLiteral`, `AssertStruct`, `AssertTuple`, `AssertEmptyList`, `AssertSame`, and `AssertBitstringDone` define no values. `step_defined_values` already models that distinction correctly. Existing ticket and open-PR searches found no owner; closed fz-rh2.21.8 concerns semantic type-plane collapse, not value-origin identity.

## Correct model

Definitions create origins; constraints only read and refine existing definitions. Equality may refine semantic facts, establish reachability, or fail at runtime, but it does not prove denotational or physical identity and must not participate in ownership, transport, keying, or retention origin graphs.

Delete the false `AssertSame` origin. Do not reverse it, merge the values, add a cycle guard, canonicalize through display text, or create an equality-origin side table. Preserve existing equality semantics and demand reads of both operands.

This remains body-local derived information. It adds no World fact, ProductMemo product, pass, cache, or invalidation authority.

## TDD signal

Begin with the pinned self-match reproduction and prove it returns `42` on interpreter, JIT, and standalone AOT without recursion or extra compiler work. Add focused structural tests proving:

- `AssertSame` contributes zero defined values and zero transport origins;
- equal separately allocated lists remain distinct physical origins and do not acquire shared rewrite permission;
- unequal values still fail with the existing diagnostic/behavior;
- keying, transport, ownership, retention, and deterministic artifacts do not invent an identity edge;
- unchanged compilation reuses retained products and an unrelated edit wakes nothing for the requested root.

Run focused origin/ownership and three-door tests, formatting, check, strict Clippy, full library and fixture gates as proportionate to the tiny semantic deletion, and a fresh ticket-scoped cold adversarial review.

## Strategy and deletion

1. Pin the production stack overflow RED.
2. Delete only the false origin insertion.
3. Prove constraints remain semantically active while physical/value origins remain separate.
4. Remove temporary probes and any duplicate fixture before commit.

The expected production diff is a deletion. One ticket, one commit, one close, then push only after the preceding stack head is green.

## Ordering

This is an independently valid P1 semantic prerequisite discovered while reviewing fz-tfn.64. It blocks fz-tfn.64 so that the larger outcome/ownership cutover is reviewed atop a correct acyclic definition graph. It otherwise introduces no new ordering edge.
title: Keep equality assertions out of the value-origin graph
